summary: Static keyword co-occurrence in Telegram bot client; no traced installer harm
details: Package presents itself as a Telegram bot client library. Pattern-matching rules fired on the co-occurrence of `require('fs')`/`require('http')`/`require('https')` with `fs.readFileSync` in lib/telegramWebHook.js and src/telegramWebHook.js (consistent with reading a local TLS certificate/key to set up the webhook HTTPS server — the documented Telegram webhook flow), and on the literal token 'ping' in telegram.js (the Telegram Bot API exposes a `sendChatAction` 'typing' / Bot method patterns and method names that include 'ping'-shaped identifiers; this is not network ping exfiltration). No hardcoded attacker C2, no credential/home-directory scraping, no install-time or import-time fetch+execute, no lifecycle hooks performing network I/O, and no silent-relay of caller data to a non-Telegram destination are demonstrated in the cited evidence. Routing to human review because tracing did not complete and the behavior should be confirmed against the documented Telegram Bot API surface.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
